# Jubilees Chapter 29 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The flight from Laban; the wrestling match at Peniel

---

**29:1** At the start of the forty-fifth jubilee — first week, first year — Jacob went to Laban to say goodbye and head home to Canaan.

**29:2** Laban gathered everyone — his flocks, his sons, his daughters — and broke down weeping as he hugged and kissed Jacob goodbye. "Please stay," he begged. "You've been good for me. God has blessed me because of you."

**29:3** Jacob wouldn't hear of it. "I need to go — my parents are waiting. Let me leave."

**29:4** Laban said farewell through tears, and Jacob was on his way.

**29:5** He sent scouts ahead to his brother Esau in the territory of Seir.

**29:6** They came back with alarming news: "We reached your brother Esau. He's on his way — with four hundred men."

**29:7** Jacob's stomach dropped. He split his company — people, flocks, herds, camels — into two separate groups.

**29:8** His logic: "If Esau attacks one group, at least the other can get away."

**29:9** Then he prayed: "LORD — God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac — you're the one who told me to come back home and promised you'd take care of me.

**29:10** I don't deserve any of this. When I first crossed the Jordan, all I had was a walking stick. Now look at me — two whole camps.

**29:11** Please — save me from my brother Esau. I'm terrified he's going to come and slaughter everyone, women and children included.

**29:12** But you made a promise: 'I'll be good to you; I'll make your descendants as countless as the sand on the seashore.'"

**29:13** That night, Jacob put together a massive peace offering for Esau: two hundred female goats, twenty male goats, two hundred ewes, twenty rams, thirty nursing camels with their young, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys, ten male donkeys.

**29:14** He divided them into separate herds with gaps between them, each in its servant's care.

**29:15** He briefed the lead servant: "When Esau meets you and asks who you belong to and where you're going,

**29:16** Tell him: 'These belong to your servant Jacob. They're a gift for his lord Esau. Jacob himself is right behind us.'"

**29:17** With everyone sent ahead, Jacob was alone. And then — out of nowhere — a man grabbed him and they wrestled through the night.

**29:18** When it became clear the man couldn't pin Jacob, he wrenched Jacob's hip out of its socket.

**29:19** "Dawn is breaking — let me go," the man said. Jacob held on: "Not until you bless me."

**29:20** "What's your name?" the man asked. "Jacob." — "Not anymore. Your name is Israel — because you've wrestled with God and with men, and you've won."

**29:21** "Now tell me your name," Jacob asked. "Why do you need to know?" the man replied. But he gave Jacob his blessing before he left.

**29:22** Jacob named the place Peniel — "Face of God" — because he said: "I looked God in the face and I'm still here."

**29:23** When the sun rose, Jacob limped away from Penuel.

**29:24** That's why the people of Israel have never eaten the sciatic nerve — the sinew attached to the hip socket — from that day to this.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The wrestling scene is the emotional climax of Jacob's story arc. The dynamic rendering preserves the terror of Jacob's anticipation of Esau (vv.7-12), the physicality of the wrestling (vv.17-21), and the etiology of the food law (v.24). Peniel/Penuel alternation follows the Ge'ez.*
